en.title: All Hail the Power of Jesus’ Name
en.author: Edward Perronet
stanzas:
[G]All hail the power of [D]Je[Em]sus’ [D]name!
Let [G]an[D]gels pros[G]trate fall;
[D]Bring forth the [G]royal dia[D]dem,
And [G]crown Him [D]Lord of [G]all.
[G]Bring forth the royal [D]diadem,
[Em]And crown Him [C]Lord [D7]of [G]all.

Crown Him, ye martyrs of your God,
Who from His altar call;
Extol the Stem of Jesse’s rod,
And crown Him Lord of all.
Extol the Stem of Jesse’s rod,
And crown Him Lord of all.

Ye seed of Israel’s chosen race,
Ye ransomed from the fall,
Hail Him who saves you by His grace,
And crown Him Lord of all.
Hail Him who saves you by His grace,
And crown Him Lord of all.

Sinners, whose love can ne’er forget
The wormwood and the gall,
Go spread your trophies at His feet,
And crown Him Lord of all.
Go spread your trophies at His feet,
And crown Him Lord of all.

Let every kindred, every tribe,
On this terrestrial ball,
To Him all majesty ascribe,
And crown Him Lord of all.
To Him all majesty ascribe,
And crown Him Lord of all.

O that, with yonder sacred throng,
We at His feet may fall,
Join in the everlasting song,
And crown Him Lord of all,
Join in the everlasting song,
And crown Him Lord of all!

notes: Perronet's poem runs to nine stanzas in the Cyber Hymnal; the six shipped here are the commonly-printed set, in Trinity Hymnal's order (p.296). Wording is the Cyber Hymnal's throughout EXCEPT stanza 5: the Cyber Hymnal has "Let every tribe and every tongue / Before Him prostrate fall / And shout in universal song / The crownèd Lord of all", while nearly every hymnal prints John Rippon's "Let every kindred, every tribe, / On this terrestrial ball, / To Him all majesty ascribe" -- Rippon's is used, taken from Timeless Truths and confirmed against the Trinity chart. Line 1 is sung as eight syllables: "power" elides to "pow'r", which is how Trinity and Timeless Truths print it; the Cyber Hymnal's fuller spelling was kept. The 8.6.8.6.8.6 meter is CORONATION's repeat of lines 3-4 written out, so stanza 1 carries chords for the repeat as well. Key G confirmed by the hymnchords.net Trinity chart. Note DIADEM and MILES LANE are the other common tunes for this text (25 and 16 hymnal instances against CORONATION's 31) and this chart will NOT fit them. SCANSION: two words are printed full and sung elided -- "power" as "pow'r" in every stanza's first line, and "every" as "ev'ry" twice in stanza 5. Both spellings are in circulation; the fuller ones are kept because that is how the source texts print them.
